display_name: Codex AI Game Studio for macOS

limitations: Shell presence does not authorize login-shell changes or command-string evaluation.
Implementations differ; launchers must remain POSIX-compatible and pass tokenized arguments.
The system Bash version can be older than Homebrew Bash and must not be assumed interchangeable.

package_managers.install_policy: Never bootstrap or update Homebrew during detection; use an exact formula/cask version only in a confirmed transaction.
Use only a verified port/version and disclose any privilege escalation in a confirmed transaction.

limitations: Metal presence does not prove that a selected model or application supports its required operations.

gpu_backends.hardware: Apple Silicon or supported AMD Mac GPU
read_only_detection: Probe torch.backends.mps.is_available in the active Python only when torch is already installed.
limitations: MPS operation coverage, numerics, memory, and performance can differ from CUDA.

read_only_detection: Check active-Python coremltools module presence without converting a model.
limitations: Module presence is not evidence that model conversion or every layer is supported.

read_only_detection: Read architecture and processor metadata without running a workload.
limitations: CPU execution can be substantially slower and may require reduced model or asset settings.

native_capabilities: read-only Darwin, macOS version, and architecture detection
native Apple Silicon and Intel project routing
Metal, MPS, Core ML, and CPU capability selection
engine and DCC application discovery without launching applications
digest-confirmed project edition selection and rollback

read_only_detection.credential_policy: Inspect environment-variable names and presence only; never read or store secret values.

adaptation_order: native source adaptation with verified license, build support, and equivalent tests
verified capability-equivalent native alternative with a comparison
hosted or manual fallback with network, privacy, cost, and reproducibility disclosure

adaptation_rules.source_constraint: Windows-only executable, DLL, MSI, or Win32 binary
adaptation_rules.preferred_native: Build a separate macOS arm64 or x86_64 implementation from verified source only when its license, dependencies, host APIs, and tests support the target.
alternatives: select a verified native macOS tool that produces the required artifact and passes the same quality gates
use a hosted or manual workflow after privacy, cost, and rights review
adaptation_rules.limitations: Windows binaries are not macOS binaries; rebuilding or replacing behavior can change output, performance, integrations, and support status.

adaptation_rules.source_constraint: Windows PowerShell script or module that depends on registry, COM, Win32, drive letters, or Windows credential stores
adaptation_rules.preferred_native: Reimplement portable behavior with Python 3 standard library or tokenized zsh/POSIX commands and documented macOS APIs.
alternatives: use the target application's native CLI, SDK, or verified MCP interface
retain the unsupported host-bound step as a documented manual handoff
adaptation_rules.limitations: Textual syntax conversion cannot reproduce Windows-only APIs; PowerShell 7 on macOS does not make Windows modules or APIs portable.

adaptation_rules.source_constraint: CUDA-only model, library, or generation pipeline
adaptation_rules.preferred_native: Use a verified Metal or MPS implementation with the same model rights, supported operations, artifact format, and quality validation.
alternatives: use a CPU implementation when measured memory and completion time are acceptable
use a hosted GPU provider after license, privacy, data-transfer, cost, and provenance review
adaptation_rules.limitations: Metal and MPS are not CUDA; unsupported operations, numerical differences, model conversions, memory pressure, and lower throughput may prevent equivalent results.

adaptation_rules.source_constraint: DirectML-only model, library, or GPU execution path
adaptation_rules.preferred_native: Use a verified Core ML, Metal, or MPS execution path that preserves supported operations, model provenance, and output quality gates.
alternatives: use a CPU backend with an explicit performance and memory estimate
choose a verified native macOS application or hosted service with equivalent artifact outputs
adaptation_rules.limitations: DirectML is a Windows API; model conversion or backend substitution can change supported layers, numerical output, speed, and memory use.

adaptation_rules.source_constraint: Windows desktop automation based on COM, UI Automation, registry, or process injection
adaptation_rules.preferred_native: Use the application's documented macOS CLI, plugin API, SDK, localhost interface, or verified MCP server with bounded permissions.
alternatives: use scoped AppleScript or Accessibility automation only after explicit permission and a dry-run plan
leave the editor action as a human-reviewed manual step
adaptation_rules.limitations: macOS Accessibility and Automation permissions are high trust, app-version-sensitive, and not equivalent to Windows automation APIs.

adaptation_rules.source_constraint: x86_64-only macOS application on an Apple Silicon host
adaptation_rules.preferred_native: Select a signed universal or arm64 build from the verified publisher and retest project, plugin, and output compatibility.
alternatives: use Rosetta only for a verified x86_64 macOS build after explicit disclosure and confirmation
choose a verified native application or manual workflow with equivalent output formats
adaptation_rules.limitations: Rosetta is a translation fallback, not native compatibility; performance, extensions, low-level drivers, and vendor support can differ.

allowed_when: the publisher provides a verified x86_64 macOS application
no universal or arm64 build satisfies the required capability
the user confirms the separate installation or invocation proposal
limitations: translation can reduce performance or increase memory use
kernel extensions, drivers, and architecture-specific plugins may remain unsupported
installation and removal are system-level actions outside edition selection

permissions: read OS, architecture, shell, GPU, disk, and application metadata without reading secret values
read the selected game project and existing MCP configuration
write only .ai-game-studio/project.json and .ai-game-studio/lock.json after full-digest confirmation
create bounded transaction backups and audit records inside the selected project
request separate confirmation for any network download, package-manager action, application control, Accessibility permission, or hosted data transfer
health_checks: confirm the host reports Darwin and the architecture is arm64 or x86_64
confirm zsh or another declared POSIX shell is available without changing the login shell
report Homebrew and MacPorts presence without bootstrapping or updating either manager
report Metal, MPS, Core ML, and CPU capability evidence without running a workload
detect Unity, Godot, Unreal, Blender, Aseprite, Pixelorama, and Tiled without launching them
validate the selected edition and descriptor digest in project.json and lock.json
uninstall: create an edition disable macos proposal and confirm its full digest before changing project state
leave external editors, package managers, MCP servers, models, and Rosetta untouched unless each has a separately confirmed uninstall plan
rollback: create an edition rollback proposal for the selected transaction and confirm its full digest
restore .ai-game-studio/project.json and .ai-game-studio/lock.json from bounded transaction backups
report separately installed external components instead of removing them implicitly
